nodes.question: What is the purpose of sulfur doping in the described process?
nodes.answer: The purpose of sulfur doping is to create a modified form of SPAC, which is referred to as S-doped SPAC.
nodes.paragraph: In the second stage, sulphur doping was performed with sulfuric acid. A certain amount of SPAC (3 g) and 30 mL of sulfuric acid diluted with pure water at a 1:3 ratio was added to a conical flask [ 35]. This mixture was hydrothermally processed in an oven at 105 C for 24 h. After this process, the obtained sample was repeatedly washed with hot and cold pure water and was named S-doped SPAC. The third stage involves adding iodine to the S-doped SPAC sample by hydrothermal heating method. To achieve iodine doping, S-doped SPAC was mixed with iodine at a 1:2 ratio in a 30 mL aqueous solution. Heating and mixing were carried out via hydrothermal processing on a magnetic stirrer at 50 C for 6 h. Subsequently, the obtained sample was washed multiple times with pure water and dried in an oven at 80 C for 2 h. This sample was named iodine@S- doped SPAC. The production scheme of the iodine@ S-doped SPAC sample is presented in Fig. 1. 2.2 Material characterization XRD analyses were performed with a Philips X'pert device with a Cu-K source.
